name: DeepInfra serverless inference
price_basis: USD per 1M TOKENS, representative model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1, observed 2026-10-14 ($0.25 in / $0.13 cached / $0.95 out, 160k ctx). DeepInfra is the LOW end of this record set on most shared models: the same-day OpenRouter table shows its Turbo tier serving llama-3.3-70b at $0.10/$0.32 - the cheapest row there - and its own page has Qwen3-235B at $0.09/$0.55, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 at $0.06/$0.18. Some models bill per inference-execution second instead of per token; the token-priced subset is what the per-mtok fields describe. Account cap: 200 concurrent requests.
notes: 2026-10-16: Artificial Analysis confirms the floor. Its Llama 3.3 70B FAQ states DeepInfra (Turbo, FP8) at $0.10 per 1M input and $0.32 per 1M output — the same split the 2026-10-14 OpenRouter table had — with a blended $0.12 per 1M, the lowest of 11 providers, and 15.2 output tok/s (20x slower than Groq's 305.7 on the same page) at 2.14s median first chunk. measured_tps moved from 14 (OpenRouter P50) to 15.2 (AA median); measured_ttft_ms moved from 510 to 2140 because the two measurements are not the same quantity (OpenRouter 'latency' vs AA 'time to first chunk'). The representative price fields stay on DeepSeek-V3.1 at $0.25/$0.95 as recorded 2026-10-14: that number was read off DeepInfra's own pricing page, which did not re-extract cleanly on 2026-10-16, so it is not silently overwritten. Measured figures are the OpenRouter 2026-10-14 P50 for DeepInfra (Turbo) on llama-3.3-70b-instruct: 0.51s latency, 14 tok/s, 99.52% uptime - the cheapest and the SLOWEST row on that table, which is exactly the price-vs-speed trade this record type exists to expose. 14 tps is shared-infrastructure Turbo, not a dedicated deployment. DeepInfra's own page states all models run on H100 or A100 GPUs. Two tiers appear on provider tables: standard and Turbo (cheaper, sometimes FP8); Artificial Analysis benchmarks them separately.
